taxonomyNote: Sources place this species in Masticophis (NatureServe, Nicholson 2025) rather than Coluber; NatureServe also notes O'Connell and Smith (2018) split populations west of the Cochise Filter Barrier as M. piceus, and renamed the English name Common Coachwhip.
fieldMarks: One of the largest North American snakes, 91-259 cm snout-vent, with smooth scales and a slender, whip-like tail.
Colour varies widely by region: dark brown front half with a red or pink belly midline (eastern), black bands broken by red bands (Sonoran), or pink, red, yellow and grey to black phases in the west.
behavior: Diurnal and solitary; active mid-morning and late afternoon but, unlike most snakes, stays active at the hottest time of day (ambient about 33 C).
Active hunter of lizards, other snakes, insects and birds and their eggs; hibernates in winter.
Active April-October in the north and mid-March to late October in Texas.
habitat: Dry, open terrain: desert, prairie, scrubland, juniper grassland, woodland, farmland, creek valleys and chaparral; terrestrial but climbs into vegetation.
Takes cover in burrows, under rocks or in vegetation.
range: Southern United States from North Carolina and Florida west through Kansas and southern Nebraska to Arizona and California (to San Francisco Bay), and north-central Mexico; not in Canada.
